17 AO No. 419 of 2025
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
None is present for the appellant.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the 
respondent no.1.
The appellants propose to challenge the 
judgment and order dated 23.04.2025, passed 
in MACP No. 20 of 2023, Smt. Kavita Devi 
Shahi and another vs. Sri Sandeep Kumar 
Bisht and others (“the claim petition”), by the 
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Additional 
District Judge, Khatima, District Udham Singh 
Nagar. By it, the appellants were awarded 
Rs.11,32,400/- as compensation alongwith 
interest @ 6 % from the date of filing of the 
claim petition. It is delayed.
Heard on Delay Condonation Application 
No. 1 of 2025.
Objections have been filed by the 
respondents.
Having heard, this Court is of the view 
that there are good grounds to condone the 
delay.
Delay condonation application is allowed.
Delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
Admit.
Call for the LCR.
List on 23.07.2026 for final hearing.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 15.05.2026
Jitendra

Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for 
the appellant in AO No.419 of 2025.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the 
appellant in AO No.306 of 2025.
It is argued on behalf of the appellant in 
AO No.419 of 2025 that the deceased had an 
Income Tax Return on 19.11.2021, but his 
compensation has not been assessed based 
on that Income Tax Return, instead, based 
on the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, 
calculation has been made. It is also 
submitted that, in fact, the death took place 
on 14.11.2022.
Fact remains that in the claim petition, 
the claimants have shown the monthly 
income of the deceased as Rs. 25,000/-. 
When confronted as to why compensation
beyond Rs.25,000/- may be assessed, 
learned counsel for the appellant seeks time. 
List this matter on 13.08.2026, along 
with the connected appeal. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
23.07.2026
RV

D35 UKHC010185932025
AO/419/2025
Smt. Kavita Devi Sahi & others
--Appellants
 Versus
United India Insurance Company Ltd. & another
--Respondents
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for the 
appellant. 
 Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the 
respondent no. 1. 
 In this appeal against an Award under the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, an application under 
Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 
1908 has been filed by the appellant so as to bring 
on record the income tax return filed by the 
deceased prior to his death.
 Learned counsel for the appellants submits 
that, in fact, the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the 
income of the deceased by not taking into 
consideration the income tax return filed by the 
deceased. But, according to him, as such the 
income tax return was not filed before the Tribunal, 
but only its acknowledgement was filed.
 Income of the deceased is to be assessed. In 
the claim petition, the deceased was earning 
Rs. 25,000/- per month, whereas it is submitted 
that as per the income tax return of the deceased of 
the previous year, his annual income was 
Rs. 4,95,000/-.  In view of the settled law, an average of 
income has to be taken. It is also settled law that 
income tax return filed post death of the deceased 
may also be taken into consideration while 
computing the income of the deceased. 
 In view of it, the income tax return that is 
proposed to be filed by the appellant may be taken 
into evidence, but before it is done, the respondents 
may be given an opportunity to file any document in 
rebuttal or to inform the Court as to whether they 
would like to adduce any evidence. 
 List on 08.10.2026. 
 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 03-09-2026
Avneet/
